citations._note: hooks/lib/__tests__/*.ts is deliberately NOT declared: those files are fixtures, the record names in them are exhibits rather than pointers, and telling the two apart is exactly the judgement a declaration exists to record. Measured before this key was written, the 45 files the three patterns above name carried 167 resolved citations, 2 dangling and 0 store-prefixed, while the 51 test files carried 21 resolved, 90 dangling and 133 store-prefixed. This clause sits inside the entry rather than in the top-level _citations note because that note is held byte-identical to the seeded template's by the drift check in hooks/lib/__tests__/config.test.ts, which cuts this whole entry out of the comparison instead.

_what: fusion's per-project configuration for THIS project. fusion reads it from the project root and merges it over fusion's own built-in defaults. Today it configures the orchestrator's Turn budget and the non-Markdown paths your project declares as citation-bearing — see _turnBudget and _citations. Keys the parser does not recognise are carried through untouched and never reported, which is why these underscore-prefixed notes can live in the file itself. The one exception is something fusion has RETIRED — a file or a key that used to configure something and no longer does. A retired file or key is reported on every guarded tool call until you delete it, because something that is inert AND silent would leave you believing a setting is in force when the mechanism behind it is gone. See _retired for the ones that exist today.
_override: To change something, add the key you want to change, in the shape fusion documents for it. The merge is per LEAF, not per object: a key you declare is taken exactly as you wrote it, and a key you leave out — even inside an object you did declare — falls straight through to fusion's built-in default. There are TWO layers, this file and those defaults. The plugin-level layer that used to sit between them, the plugin's own hooks/config.json, is gone with the guard settings it carried, so nothing stands between what you write here and what fusion ships. So {"orchestrator": {"maxTurns": 12}} sets the Turn budget and touches nothing else, and a leaf you omit is fusion's own value rather than something inherited from an install. A value with the wrong type is dropped and named in an advisory, then inherits as if you had omitted it; a file that is not valid JSON is dropped and reported the same way, never ignored in silence.
_turnBudget: The Turn budget is one of the things this file configures; the citation-path declaration in _citations is the other. "orchestrator": {"maxTurns": 12} is the number of Turns the orchestrator's Phase-2 loop may run before its Max-Turns circuit breaker exits the loop and reports what is left. It merges by the per-leaf rule in _override, and it is read once per session by bin/fusion-turn-budget at the orchestrator's Setup — no hook reads it. fusion's own budget is defined in exactly one place, the DEFAULTS in the plugin's hooks/lib/config.ts, and is deliberately not restated in any shipped JSON file or in any agent prompt, so this file is the only place a project changes it. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more — 0, a negative, a decimal, a string — is dropped and named in an advisory, then inherits as if it were absent; there is no upper bound, because a project that wants 60 Turns has said so in a git-tracked file.
_citations: Which of your NON-MARKDOWN files carry record citations is something only your project knows, so your project declares it here and fusion detects nothing. "citations": {"extraPaths": ["src/**/*.go", "internal/*.py"]} names the files that bin/fusion-citation-check and bin/fusion-citation-sweep read IN ADDITION to the Markdown they already read. Each entry is a git pathspec evaluated under :(glob), so * does not cross a / and ** does, and it is resolved against the files git tracks — an untracked or an ignored file is never named by one. Declaring a file is a judgement you make and not one fusion can make for you: outside Markdown there is no code fence and no block quote, so fusion cannot tell a token that POINTS at a record from one that merely shows what a record name looks like, and inside a file you declare it reads every such token as a pointer. Declare the files that cite records, and leave out the ones that exhibit them. DECLARE NOTHING AND YOU GET [], which is exactly today's behaviour: the Markdown corpus alone, no extra files, no advisory. The value must be an array of strings with none of them empty; anything else is dropped WHOLE and named in an advisory, then inherits as if you had omitted it, so one bad entry never leaves half a declaration in force.
_retired: If your project root still carries a fusion-guard.json, this file replaces it and fusion no longer reads a byte of it. COPY YOUR TURN BUDGET ACROSS FIRST if that file set one: {"orchestrator": {"maxTurns": 12}} belongs here now, and a budget left behind is not read — the orchestrator falls back to fusion's built-in default without saying so, which is the one loss of this migration you would not notice. Then delete fusion-guard.json, and the advisory naming it stops. Copy nothing else across. Everything else that file carried configured the guard, which decides nothing any more, and the four top-level keys that held it — guard, decisions, escalation and, since 260824, churn — are each reported here as retired if they turn up in this file, until you delete them.
_gitTracked: This file belongs in version control, and that is the point of it living at the project root. It decides how many Turns the orchestrator may run against your project — so every change to it has to appear in a diff and pass through the same review as the rest of the project. The diff is now the ONLY thing that bounds it. fusion used to defend this file against its own agents: the guard added it to the protected list as soon as it existed and wrote back any change an agent made to it. That defence went with the protected-path mechanism, so an agent can edit this file like any other, and the git history is where you see that one did.
